title: DraftKings Faces Increasing Competition in Prediction Markets | DKNG Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits DraftKings after a fall of more than 40% in 2026, driven by prediction-market competitors Polymarket and Kalshi taking share. Before prediction markets, DraftKings was steadily winning state-by-state sports-betting approvals; the new entrants bypassed that framework and offered products nationally, forcing DraftKings to shift strategy and launch its own prediction-markets product, which management says has gained momentum surprisingly fast. Revenue grew from $500 million in 2020 to about $6 billion, but growth has since stagnated and trailing twelve-month revenue has slipped below its $6.2 billion peak, while the operating-cash-flow-to-sales improvement since 2022 has also stalled. Sentiment has turned so sour that the forward price-to-earnings ratio of about 12 prices in essentially zero growth over the next several years. His updated discounted cash flow value is about $31 per share against a market price a little over $20, near the 52-week low. He reiterates DraftKings as a buying opportunity, firmer than his conditional buy of 6 October, but admits he is losing confidence in near-term execution and that convincing investors will take longer. Call: DKNG — BUY (strengthened from CONDITIONAL_BUY). Bull case: tighter prediction-market regulation would favour DraftKings' licensed position. Bear case: fading near-term execution confidence and a longer wait for investor conviction.
